## Disposition and explicit limits

Accept a credited **PARTIAL prior resolution** of Santos Question 5, 30000813 / OWR-1595-005, from Nikita Lebedev, *Integrality, smoothness and normality bounds for cube-truncated Hadamard simplices*, [arXiv:2609.32950v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32950v1). The [original Santos report](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46125) supplies the original family and question.

The complete authored audit accepts all seventeen written proof arguments. The smallest nonintegral dimension is 11. Smoothness holds exactly when m > (d-1)n/2 and m/n is not an odd integer. Every member in the strict upper range is normal, including nonsmooth resonances, and further sufficient normality bands are accepted. The complete normality classification remains unresolved. The complement of these positive bands contains known negative examples and families and must not be called entirely open. Hypotheses retain the marked Hadamard simplex and full affine degree lattices.

**Official Lean statement/provenance inspection was static only. No Lean compiler, downloaded proof code, author verification script, author mutation script or dependency installer was executed.** No independent Lean kernel certificate, peer-review endorsement, new substantive turn or novelty claim is made. The inspected public record identifies a preprint submitted 26 September 2026; no journal reference or peer-review acceptance was stated there. Source-disclosed AI assistance is recorded without substituting for mathematical review.

## Authored mathematics and fresh diagnostics

All nine accepted public audit files are byte-preserved under current/, including the full audit, independently authored exact checker and public source/static-statement metadata. Source documents, manuscript/source text, archive contents, Lean companion contents, datasets, private sources, private coordination and identifying metadata for excluded private files are excluded. Public URLs, titles, hashes, byte counts and historical inspection/retrieval records remain metadata only. No source download or Lean installation is needed for public reproduction.

The fresh wrapper enforces all 35 diagnostic identities and exactly 496 invocations per interpreter mode, including six explicitly identified embedded negative-predicate checks. Eight additional mathematical mutations fail at their intended condition; one forced false condition is a separately labeled injected-failure control. These controls modify only our authored checker in memory. The author's 29 mutation outcomes are not reproduced. Finite diagnostics cannot establish the seventeen general theorems or classify the residual normality region; the accepted written proof audit carries those claims.

Normal, -O and -OO are freshly tested with actual UID=EUID=1000, -I -S -B, mode 0444 files and 0555 directories. All complete raw stdout/stderr bytes and recursive exact JSON types/values match mode-specific pinned references without normalization. Empty, skipped or expected-failure output cannot replace a positive suite. Explicit control identities/counts and exact intended integrity/mathematical rejection reasons are enforced. Changed details, extra output, nested bool/int or float/int substitutions, wrong mode, altered references and unexpected stderr are tested. Hostile imports and startup hooks remain inactive, and the full hostile baseline equals the clean baseline.

Each mode records 42 whole-packet physical EACCES denials, plus two input-denial probes in the mathematical wrapper; 57 integrity negatives; 70 schema/acceptance negatives; and 42 comparator negatives. These infrastructure controls are not mathematical mutations. Whole-inventory before/after byte hashes are unchanged. The additive diff is also reconstructed in a fresh location and its complete positive baseline outputs match the final sealed baseline in all three modes.

The tested standard-library interpreter is CPython 3.12.14 and is trusted, not authenticated. Read-only Unix modes are an accidental-write barrier, not kernel immutability or protection against intentional owner chmod.

Historical current/VERIFICATION_RECEIPT.json, current/AUDIT_MANIFEST.json and PREPARATION_* evidence are bound by the final manifest. They are not final trust anchors. current/verify_audit_packet.py is preserved but its historical harness replay is NOT_RUN here. Also NOT_RUN: new source search, excluded source-body replay, dataset replay, Lean build, Lean kernel axiom audit, downloaded companion execution and author mutation controls. Final sealed receipts stay outside their own bound inventory, preventing circular self-hashing.

## Exact scope and independent pins

This draft adds exactly 40 files (499,948 bytes) under unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30000813. No QUEUE or unrelated changes. Base commit: 6ca1e663ab556636a3c2a9b67a96274ef95e8bab; base tree: a675bbb4eb340ad8a83943d490404c5f9585c0e1. Suggested branch: audit/truncated-hadamard-30000813-prior.

Authenticate BOOTSTRAP.py against the independent SHA-256 below before execution. Save that authenticated copy outside the packet. With packet files 0444, directories 0555 and actual UID=EUID=1000, run python -I -S -B /trusted/BOOTSTRAP.py --controls /path/to/packet, then repeat with -O and -OO. README.md gives the positive-only commands. No private archive or source body is required. The bootstrap authenticates the entire delivered inventory, including acceptance and all historical/pre-seal receipts; the following fixed hashes are supplied out of band in this PR description.

- BOOTSTRAP.py: 7794638ce40e0f73a0823a0940e3abed0aaf6b28fa532835d210c4a90b139753 (2849 bytes)

title: Audit Hadamard truncations: credited partial prior resolution
